summary: BioAstro is a real-time biomedical monitoring and decision-support software platform designed for two-astronaut crews operating pressurized lunar rovers during long-duration missions (30 days to 1 year).The system addresses the challenge by integrating two critical NASA Human Research Program risks: the neurological and behavioral impact of prolonged isolation and confinement (cognitive fatigue, apathy, and stress), and bone density loss in lunar gravity 1/6G. Driven by a state machine that synchronizes the daily operational cycle without overburdening crew members with invasive surveys, the current prototype functions as a digital twin combining passive rover behavioral telemetry (processed via digital filters), ultra-brief psychometric assessments, simulated quantitative ultrasound (QUS) data, urinary biomarkers, and mechanical load tracking. Its ergonomic color-coded alerts (Sage Green, Warm Amber, and Coral) guide immediate preventive or corrective actions onboard.For future mission deployment, its modular JSON-based architecture is ready for plug-and-play integration with physical wearable biosensors, live vehicle telemetry buses, and delay-tolerant clinical reporting to flight surgeons on Earth.
details:
BioAstro: Integrated Cognitive, Behavioral, and Bone Health Monitoring System for Pressurized Lunar Rovers

1. Executive Summary and Scope

BioAstro is a real-time biomedical monitoring and decision-support software platform designed for 2-astronaut crews operating a Pressurized Lunar Rover during long-duration lunar missions (30 days to 1 year) under lunar gravity (1/6 G = 1.62 m/s²).

Inside these mobile habitats, the crew lives in a confined cabin alternating between prolonged periods of sedentary driving and high-demand extravehicular activities (EVAs). BioAstro integrates two critical spaceflight health domains that are traditionally addressed in silos:

  1. Neurological, Cognitive, and Behavioral Health (Isolation and Confinement): Detects accumulated fatigue, apathy from sensory monotony, and acute stress caused by prolonged confinement before they compromise driving safety or EVA operations.
  2. Bone Health and Mechanical Loading (Altered Gravity): Monitors bone demineralization induced by lunar hypogravity (1/6 G) and prolonged cabin sitting, dynamically adjusting preventive physical routines onboard.

Justification based on NASA standards: Within NASA’s Human Research Roadmap (HRP), this scenario directly addresses the BMed risk (Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Conditions and Psychiatric Disorders, featuring a critical isolation inflection point starting at month five / Mission Day 150) as well as NASA's Design Reference Mission (DRM) risk matrix ratings for long-duration Lunar Orbital + Surface missions (3×3 in Operations and 4×2 in Long-Term Health, classified as "Requires Characterization"), where early detection and crew autonomy are essential.

2. Technical Architecture and Operation

The current prototype operates as a 100% software-based modular digital twin (requiring no external physical hardware for validation), with interfaces structured around standardized JSON schemas ready for future plug-and-play connection with wearable biosensors and real vehicle telemetry buses.

2.1. Unified Temporal Core (MissionClockFSM)

To prevent operational inconsistencies (such as prompting questionnaires while driving) and reduce administrative workload, a cyclic Finite State Machine (MissionClockFSM) governs both subsystems in compressed time (TIME_SCALE = 900, where 1 real second = 15 simulated minutes, with manual override controls in the UI):

  • HABITAT_PRE_EVA (120 min): Habitat wake-up. Enables the brief sleep questionnaire and, when triggered by schedule or low sleep score, the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT-B) before authorizing rover departure.
  • ROVER_ACTIVE (300 min): Surface exploration. Runs passive driving behavioral simulation, automatically logs sedentary vehicle driving hours (horas_conduccion) for the bone module, and blocks non-critical visual popups on the helmet display (hud_notifications_allowed = False).
  • AIRLOCK_TRANSITION (10 min): Airlock repressurization. Optimal window for the brief emotional check-in (I-PANAS-SF), while blocking fine-motor reaction tests (PVT-B) due to pressurized gloves.
  • HABITAT_RECOVERY (1010 min): Base recovery. Logs completed EVA duration (minutos_eva), manages lighting/decompression protocols, schedules in-cabin resistive exercise sessions, and triggers periodic clinical evaluations.

2.2. Neurological, Cognitive, and Behavioral Subsystem

Combines passive behavioral telemetry with ultra-brief psychometric assessments calibrated against each astronaut's individual baseline:

  1. Passive Behavioral Telemetry and DSP Filtering (RoverBehavioralSimulator):
    • Models daily progression of latent fatigue (fatigue_level) and apathy (apathy_level) via discrete Euler integration (x[k+1] = x[k] + x_dot[k] × Δt), incorporating sleep debt and a non-linear deterioration term starting on Mission Day 150.
      • Steering Jerk Index (steering_jerk_index): Normalized RMS of |a[k] - a[k-1]| / Δt over a 10-sample sliding window (alert threshold > 0.65).
      • Route Completion (objectives_completed_pct): Percentage of scheduled scientific sampling stations completed (alert threshold < 75%).
      • Return Pace Ratio (avg_return_speed_ratio): Speed ratio v_actual / v_nominal during the final 30% of the return leg (alert threshold > 1.20).
    • Pre-Rover Sleep Questionnaire: 4 factual self-report items (< 20 s) covering sleep latency, awakenings, wake inertia, and disruption cause (sleep_questionnaire_score, 0–100 scale).
    • Brief Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT-B): 15–20 s reaction test with randomized inter-stimulus intervals (1.5–4.5 s) classifying valid responses (100–500 ms), attentional lapses (L_actual > 500 ms), and false starts (FS_actual < 100 ms).
    • I-PANAS-SF Affective Scale: 10 post-EVA items measuring Positive Affect (PA) and Negative Affect (NA) independently. Includes an automated survey fatigue detector: if rushed responses (< 600 ms/item) or zero variance (variance = 0) are detected, subjective surveys are suspended for 48 hours (survey_fatigue_cooldown) and assessment relies exclusively on passive rover telemetry and PVT.
    • Synthesizes rectified attentional (P_PVT), affective (P_affect), and behavioral (P_behavior) penalties into a 0–100 score: CRI_linear = 100 - (40 × P_PVT + 35 × P_affect + 25 × P_behavior)
    • To prevent high performance in one area from masking a critical failure in another, a non-linear safety interlock automatically caps the index at CRI_final ≤ 55 if any isolated critical threshold is exceeded: L_actual ≥ 5, FS_actual ≥ 3, or ΔNA ≥ +7.

2.3. Bone Health and Mechanical Loading Subsystem

Evaluates skeletal structural and metabolic integrity by combining simulated clinical telemetry with operational durations imported from MissionClockFSM:

  1. Quantitative Ultrasound (QUS):
    • Simulates portable calcaneal/tibial densitometry readings (modeled after Lunar Achilles Express / Sunlight MiniOmni / Echolight REMS) using Speed of Sound (SOS, normal range 1530–1600 m/s, risk < 1500 m/s) and Broadband Ultrasound Attenuation (BUA, normal range 75–95 dB/MHz, risk < 65 dB/MHz) to compute the Stiffness Index (SI) and T-Score: SI = (0.67 × BUA) + (0.28 × SOS) - 420 T-Score = (SI - SI_ref) / SD_ref
    • Simulates portable microfluidic urine analyzers (normalized to creatinine) to detect early bone resorption before structural density loss becomes visible:
      • Urinary Calcium (CaU): Normal range 100–250 mg/day (10–20 mg/dL); risk > 250 mg/day.
      • C-Terminal Telopeptide (CTX): Normal range 100–400 μg/mmol creatinine; risk > 500 μg/mmol creatinine.
      • Using both biomarkers and activity history, the model estimates the Monthly Bone Loss Rate (TPM, in %/month).
    • Integrates sedentary rover driving hours and EVA minutes (imported from MissionClockFSM) with daily logged in-cabin resistive training (t_ex, load factor F_load / F_ref) and pre-approved nutritional supplementation (Calcium/Vitamin D): ICM = min(100, 100 × [ (w_EVA × t_EVA) + (w_ex × t_ex × (F_load / F_ref)) ] / C_daily_target)
    • If ICM < 75% for 3 consecutive days, the Inactivity_Detected = True flag is triggered and the projected TPM slope increases.

2.4. Unified Decision Engine, Cross-Coupling, and Color Coding

Both subsystems share a non-intrusive ergonomic interface governed by a Global Priority Rule (the main dashboard status always displays the highest active severity level across both modules):

  • Level 1: Nominal — Sage Green (#2EE59D)
    • Trigger Conditions:
      • Cognitive: CRI_final ≥ 80, sleep ≥ 60, steering_jerk_index ≤ 0.65, route ≥ 75%, and return ratio ≤ 1.20.
      • Bone: T-Score > -1.0, TPM < 0.5%/month, ICM ≥ 75%, and active supplementation.
      • Displays the full green wellness ring and authorizes standard rover/EVA operations.
      • Logs adaptive adherence milestones (gamification) without intrusive popups.
      • Maintains nominal schedule: tactical check-ins every 2–3 sorties and full clinical evaluation (PSQI + PANAS-20 + QUS) every 30 ± 7 days.
    • Trigger Conditions:
      • Cognitive: 60 ≤ CRI_final ≤ 79, ΔPA ≤ -5 (apathy), ΔNA ≥ +4 (post-EVA load), sleep < 60, DSP telemetry anomaly, or mission_day ≥ 150.
      • Bone: -1.9 ≤ T-Score ≤ -1.0 (osteopenia), 0.5% ≤ TPM ≤ 1.0%/month, or 3 days with Inactivity_Detected = True.
      • Cross-Coupling: High stress (cortisol) triggers preventive bone alerts; physical prescriptions adjust cognitive recovery windows.
      • Displays calm, actionable recommendations without blaming the crew.
      • If sleep < 60, requires PVT-B completion before authorizing ROVER_ACTIVE.
      • Recommends a 20-minute resistance band routine in cabin; if triggered by cognitive stress/fatigue, splits the routine into short 10-minute low-mental-load blocks.
      • Escalates monitoring frequency to every 48h (ELEVATED_WATCH).
    • Trigger Conditions:
      • Cognitive: CRI_final < 60 or non-linear safety veto active (CRI_cap = 55 due to L_actual ≥ 5, FS_actual ≥ 3, or ΔNA ≥ +7).
      • Bone: T-Score ≤ -2.0 (NASA-STD-3001 maximum permissible limit before high fracture risk) or sustained TPM > 1.0%/month.
      • Operational Role Swap: Suggests switching the affected crew member to co-pilot/navigation duties, handing over active rover driving and deferring non-critical EVAs.
      • In-Cabin Intervention: Immediate 25-minute decompression break with lighting/acoustic regulation and gradual restructuring of the resistive mechanical loading plan.
      • Ground Telemetry: Automatically generates and transmits the Consolidated Clinical Sheet (CRI, PVT-B, DSP, T-Score, CaU, CTX, and load history) to flight surgeons on Earth.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Languages and Mathematical Engines: Python (with NumPy) and JavaScript (Node.js / Express) to implement simulation engines (Euler integration of fatigue/apathy, QUS acoustic modeling, and matrix calculations for CRI, SI, ICM, and TPM).
  • Digital Signal Processing (DSP): Algorithmic implementation of transient rejection filters (Slew-Rate Gate) and Savitzky-Golay polynomial smoothing to filter lunar terrain vibration noise.
  • Backend Architecture and Interoperability: Modular REST API design (FastAPI / Express) and standardized JSON data contracts ready for real sensor ingestion.
  • User Interface (UI/UX): Interactive web application (BioAstro Dashboard) designed with a low-visual-fatigue ergonomic palette (Sage Green, Warm Amber, Soft Coral, and Cyan Mist) adapted to cabin lighting conditions.
  • Hardware: Zero physical hardware built. We intentionally opted for a high-fidelity software simulation and algorithmic validation architecture grounded in clinical and operational parameters from the NASA Human Research Roadmap (OSDR, HERA, Desert RATS, and TBone studies) and spaceflight QUS/microfluidics standards.

4. Creativity and Innovation

  1. Passive Psychological Detection via Vehicle Dynamics: Instead of interrupting astronauts with constant questionnaires, BioAstro turns the rover's steering wheel into a passive behavioral sensor, extracting micro-variations in motor impulsivity or apathy (steering_jerk_index) after filtering lunar terrain vibrations with DSP.
  2. Bidirectional Psycho-Biomechanical Coupling: Bridges two domains that normally operate independently: it accounts for how chronic stress (cortisol elevation) accelerates bone loss and lowers exercise adherence, automatically adapting physical workout duration and intensity based on daily cognitive readiness.
  3. Anti-Bias and Anti-Fatigue Architecture: Features a non-linear safety veto (CRI_cap = 55) that prevents arithmetic averages from hiding critical attentional lapses, paired with a mechanical-response detector (< 600 ms) that automatically suspends surveys when user saturation is detected.

5. Factors Considered by the Team

  • Ergonomics and Spacesuit Constraints: Smart lockout of fine-motor touchscreen tests during airlock transitions (AIRLOCK_TRANSITION) due to pressurized gloves, and suppression of non-critical alerts during active driving (ROVER_ACTIVE).
  • Medical Ethics and Crew Autonomy: The software never issues definitive medical diagnoses or prescribes pharmaceuticals on its own; it guides preventive/corrective exercise habits and pre-approved nutrition onboard while escalating the Consolidated Clinical Sheet to flight surgeons on Earth when critical thresholds are crossed.
  • Lunar Hypogravity Physiology (1/6 G): Distinguishes between the actual mechanical loading of a lunar surface walk (EVA) versus prolonged sedentary driving inside the cabin, avoiding the assumption that partial gravity alone preserves bone mass.
  • Temporal Dynamics of Isolation: Explicitly models the neurobehavioral inflection point starting on Mission Day 150 and balances daily tactical monitoring with deep clinical evaluations every 30 ± 7 days.

6. Benefits, Intended Impact, and Future Implementation

Current Operational and Clinical Benefits

  • Proactive Accident Prevention: Reduces the risk of navigation or driving errors on uneven lunar terrain caused by attentional lapses or sleep debt.
  • Early Subclinical Detection: Identifies both latent mood deterioration and early bone resorption (via CaU and CTX) weeks before they escalate into behavioral crises or fractures from severe osteopenia (T-Score ≤ -2.0).
  • Zero Cognitive Overload: Minimizes survey fatigue through passive inference, cross-subsystem synchronization, and non-alarmist visual alerts.

Future Implementation Roadmap (Scalability to Real Missions)

To transition BioAstro from a simulation prototype into an operational system for sustained lunar exploration (such as Artemis pressurized rovers), its modular architecture prepares the following expansion phases:

  1. Plug-and-Play Integration with Real Biosensors: Replacing simulated datasets via existing JSON contracts to connect via Bluetooth/USB with portable QUS bone densitometers (Lunar Achilles Express, Sunlight MiniOmni, Echolight REMS), Lab-on-a-Chip microfluidic urine analyzers (LOCAD / rHEALTH), force-sensing insoles (Novel Pedar / Loadsol), and digital resistance-band dynamometers (Activ5).
  2. Direct Vehicle Telemetry Bus Connection: Live ingestion of accelerometers, steering angle, and odometry from the pressurized rover while keeping the existing DSP conditioning pipeline intact.
  3. Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) with Earth: Asynchronous automated transmission of the Consolidated Clinical Sheet to flight surgeons on Earth during deep-space communication windows.
  4. Predictive Calibration and Full HRP Risk Coverage: Integrating machine learning models to personalize individual crew baselines and expanding monitoring to the remaining three NASA Human Research Program hazards (space radiation, distance from Earth, and hostile closed environments).
